This polity's capital was sacked during a civil war by Ivar the Boneless. One ruler of this kingdom converted both himself and his priest Colfi to Christianity due to a missionary named Paulinus. The Codex Amiatinus was prepared in this polity as a gift to the Pope in its city of Jarrow, and St. Cuthbert helped grow its monasteries at Melrose and Lindisfarne. This kingdom saw a dispute between the Celtic faction led by Colman and Hilda and the Roman faction led by St. Wilfrid resolved at the Synod of Whitby. At a battle fought near the Winwaed River, forces under its king, Oswiu, killed Penda, a king of its rival, Mercia. Name this member of the Heptarchy containing York, with a directional name.

Dissidents suppressed during this man's tenure included Joseph Brodsky. In his successful bid for power, this man's co-conspirator was Nikolai Podgornyi. In one speech, this man declared an "alliance of the working class with science" to oppose the reform program of Aleksei Kosygin. Earlier, Kosygin and this man had shared power in a "collective leadership." While in office, this man negotiated the second SALT treaty with Jimmy Carter and dispatched troops to resist the mujahideen in Afghanistan. He had earlier dispatched Soviet forces to put down the Prague Spring as implementation of his namesake "Doctrine" declaring the right of intervention when socialism was threatened. Yuri Andropov succeeded this man after his 1982 death. Name this General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who succeeded Nikita Khrushchev.
